get_resource.description: Read one Wikiversity page as plain text, along with its list of sections, so a later step can summarise it, translate it or turn it into a lesson plan. Narrow to one section to pull just the exercises or just the reading list. A hub page such as a School or a Portal is a shelf of links rather than prose, so it comes back with no text; List what a course contains is the action for those.

mock_response.text:
Introduction

All cells need energy, the ability to perform or complete work, in order for them to maintain their existence.
mock_response.title: Photosynthesis

list_lessons.description: The syllabus: every lesson, unit and further resource a course, school, portal or topic holds, in the order the page itself puts them in. Wikiversity builds a course two ways, as pages filed beneath it and as a page of links to resources elsewhere, and this reads both, so a course comes back whole whichever way it was built. Each part says whether it has been written yet, so the gaps in a course are visible too.
